spec: Calculate the extension and retraction forces of a pneumatic air cylinder. Write an entry function `force(pressure, dimensions)` where the first is the operating air pressure in bar and the second is a tuple of the bore diameter and the rod diameter in millimeters. First, convert the pressure from bar to megapascals by dividing by ten. Next, calculate the bore area and the annular area, which is the bore area minus the rod area, using the formula pi times radius squared. Finally, calculate the extension force by multiplying the bore area by the pressure in megapascals, and the retraction force by multiplying the annular area by the pressure. Return both forces in newtons. Example: given 6 bar and diameters of (50, 20), calculate the respective extending and retracting forces in newtons.

title: Climbing Route Difficulty Grader
spec: Assign a difficulty grade to an indoor climbing route based on its holds and wall angle. Write an entry function `grade(holds, angle)` where the first is the number of holds and the second is the wall overhang angle in degrees. The base difficulty starts at five. Add two to the difficulty if the wall angle exceeds twenty degrees. Subtract one for every ten holds present on the route, as more holds make it easier. The final difficulty must be clamped to a minimum of one and a maximum of ten. Return the calculated difficulty score. Example: given 25 holds and an angle of 30, the base 5 plus 2 minus 2 yields a difficulty of 5.

title: Welding Heat Input Calculator
spec: Estimate the heat input and cooling time for an arc welding process. Write an entry function `weld(current, voltage)` where the first is the welding current in amperes and the second is the arc voltage. Assume a constant travel speed of five millimeters per second and a thermal efficiency factor of zero point eight. First, calculate the arc power by multiplying current by voltage. Then calculate the heat input per millimeter by multiplying the power by the efficiency factor, and dividing by the travel speed. Finally, determine the cooling time from eight hundred to five hundred degrees Celsius by dividing the heat input by fifty. Return the heat input and the cooling time. Example: given a current of 150 and voltage of 20, the power is 3000, heat input is 480, and cooling time is 9.6 seconds.

title: Ski Lift Cable Sag Estimator
spec: Calculate the sag of a ski lift cable between two support towers. Write an entry function `cable(span, tension)` where the first is the horizontal distance between towers in meters and the second is the cable tension in newtons. Assume the cable has a uniform weight of forty newtons per meter. Determine the total weight of the suspended cable by multiplying the span by the linear weight. Next, approximate the midpoint sag by multiplying the weight per meter by the square of the span, then dividing by eight times the tension. Return the total cable weight and the midpoint sag in meters. Example: given a span of 100 and a tension of 20000, the weight is 4000 and the sag is 2.5 meters.

title: Olive Oil Extraction Yield
spec: Calculate the expected yield of extra virgin olive oil from a harvest batch. Write an entry function `press(mass, moisture)` where the first is the mass of harvested olives in kilograms and the second is the moisture content percentage. First, determine the dry mass by subtracting the moisture percentage from one hundred, dividing by one hundred, and multiplying by the total mass. Assume the dry mass contains twenty five percent extractable oil. Calculate the oil volume in liters knowing that olive oil has a density of zero point nine kilograms per liter. Return the dry mass and the expected oil volume. Example: given 1000 kilograms of olives with 60 percent moisture, the dry mass is 400, giving 100 kilograms of oil, which is 111.1 liters.

title: Hydronic Heating Flow Calculator
spec: Determine the required water flow rate to heat a set of rooms. Write an entry function `flow(loads, drop)` where the first is a list of heat loads for different rooms in watts and the second is the temperature drop across the radiators in degrees Celsius. Calculate the total heat load by summing the list. Determine the required total mass flow rate of water by dividing the total heat load by the product of the temperature drop and the specific heat capacity of water, which is four thousand one hundred eighty four. Convert this flow rate to liters per minute by multiplying by sixty. Return the total load and the flow rate in liters per minute. Example: given loads of 1000 and 1500, and a drop of 10, the total load is 2500 and the flow rate is 0.358 liters per minute.

title: Sailboat Capsize Screening Formula
spec: Evaluate the capsize risk of a sailboat based on its dimensions. Write an entry function `stability(beam, displacement)` where the first is the beam width in feet and the second is the boat displacement in pounds. First, convert the displacement into cubic feet of seawater by dividing by sixty four. Then calculate the capsize screening value by dividing the beam by the cube root of the displacement volume. A value less than two indicates a boat suitable for offshore sailing. Return the calculated screening value and a boolean indicating if it is offshore capable. Example: given a beam of 10 and displacement of 10000, the volume is 156.25 and the screening value is 1.85, so it is capable.

title: Compost Carbon Nitrogen Ratio
spec: Calculate the overall carbon to nitrogen ratio for a compost pile. Write an entry function `compost(greens, browns)` where both inputs are masses in kilograms. The first input represents green materials which have a carbon to nitrogen ratio of fifteen to one and a moisture content of eighty percent. The second input represents brown materials with a ratio of fifty to one and moisture of ten percent. Calculate the dry mass of each component, then determine the total carbon and total nitrogen contributions assuming total parts sum to the ratio plus one. Return the overall carbon to nitrogen ratio of the combined pile. Example: given 10 kilograms of greens and 5 kilograms of browns, compute and return the resulting blended ratio as a float.

title: Film Development Time Adjuster
spec: Adjust the baseline development time for photographic film based on temperature and push processing. Write an entry function `develop(base, temperature)` where the first is the baseline time at twenty degrees Celsius in minutes, and the second is the actual chemical temperature. For every degree above twenty, decrease the time by five percent of the baseline. For every degree below twenty, increase it by five percent. Then apply a push process adjustment that adds two minutes to the time. Return the final adjusted development time. Example: given a base time of 10 and a temperature of 22, the time decreases by 1 minute, plus 2 for pushing, resulting in 11 minutes.

title: Pasture Grazing Capacity
spec: Estimate how many days a pasture can support a herd of livestock. Write an entry function `graze(area, intake)` where the first is the pasture area in hectares and the second is the daily forage intake per animal in kilograms. Assume the pasture yields two thousand kilograms of usable dry matter per hectare. Calculate the total available forage by multiplying the area by the yield. Then determine the number of grazing days for a standard herd of fifty animals by dividing the total forage by the product of the intake and the herd size. Return the total forage and the grazing days. Example: given an area of 5 and an intake of 12, the total forage is 10000 and grazing days is 16.6.

title: Ultrasonic Flaw Detection
spec: Evaluate the depth and size of a structural flaw using ultrasonic testing. Write an entry function `scan(time, amplitude)` where the first is the echo return time in microseconds and the second is the echo signal amplitude as a percentage. First calculate the depth of the flaw knowing the speed of sound in steel is five thousand nine hundred meters per second; the distance is the speed multiplied by half the return time, converting microseconds to seconds. Next evaluate the severity of the flaw: if the amplitude exceeds fifty percent, the flaw is considered critical. Return the flaw depth in millimeters and a boolean indicating if it is critical. Example: given a time of 10 and amplitude of 60, the depth is 29.5 millimeters and it is critical.

title: Indoor Arena Air Purifier
spec: Calculate the number of air purification units required for an indoor sports arena. Write an entry function `purify(volume, attendees)` where the first is the interior volume of the arena in cubic meters and the second is the expected number of people. The base air circulation requirement is two volume changes per hour. Each attendee adds an additional requirement of zero point five cubic meters per hour. Calculate the total required airflow by summing these two requirements. Determine the number of purification units needed by dividing the total airflow by the capacity of a standard unit, which is two thousand cubic meters per hour, rounded up to the nearest whole number. Return the total airflow and the unit count. Example: given a volume of 50000 and 1000 attendees, the base is 100000, plus 500 makes 100500, requiring 51 units.

title: Snowmobile Track Flotation
spec: Evaluate the deep snow flotation of a snowmobile based on track dimensions and rider weight. Write an entry function `float(weight, dimensions)` where the first is the combined weight of the snowmobile and rider in kilograms and the second is a tuple containing the track width and length in centimeters. First, calculate the track footprint area in square centimeters. Then, convert the total weight to a force in newtons by multiplying by nine point eight. Calculate the ground pressure by dividing the force by the footprint area. Determine if the setup is suitable for deep powder, which requires a pressure below zero point zero five newtons per square centimeter. Return the footprint area, the pressure, and the suitability boolean. Example: given weight 250 and dimensions (40, 350), the area is 14000, force is 2450, pressure is 0.175, returning False.

title: Saffron Yield Estimator
spec: Estimate the harvest labor and final dried spice mass for a saffron crop. Write an entry function `harvest(flowers, workers)` where the first is the total number of harvested crocus flowers and the second is the number of available workers. Assume each flower yields three stigmas, and it takes one hundred fifty stigmas to produce one gram of fresh saffron. The dried saffron mass is twenty percent of the fresh mass. Calculate the time required to process the flowers assuming one worker can process two thousand flowers per hour. Return the dried saffron mass in grams and the total processing time in hours. Example: given 30000 flowers and 5 workers, the dried mass is 120.0 grams and it takes 3.0 hours.

title: Koi Pond Filtration Capacity
spec: Assess if a mechanical and biological filtration system can support a koi pond. Write an entry function `pond(volume, koi)` where the first is the pond volume in gallons and the second is the number of adult koi fish. Each adult koi requires two hundred fifty gallons of water to remain healthy. The filter must be able to turn over the entire pond volume one point five times per hour. Calculate the minimum required pump flow rate in gallons per hour. Then determine if the pond volume is large enough to support the number of koi. Return the required pump flow rate and a boolean for the volume check. Example: given a volume of 2000 and 6 koi, the flow rate is 3000 and the volume is sufficient since 6 times 250 is 1500.

title: Microscope Resolution Calculator
spec: Evaluate the total magnification and resolving power of a compound microscope. Write an entry function `resolve(objective, eyepiece)` where the first is a tuple of the objective lens magnification and numerical aperture, and the second is the eyepiece magnification. First calculate the total magnification by multiplying the objective and eyepiece magnifications. Then calculate the resolving power in nanometers using the Rayleigh criterion, assuming a light wavelength of five hundred fifty nanometers. The resolving power is zero point six one times the wavelength, divided by the numerical aperture. Return the total magnification and the resolving power. Example: given an objective of (40, 0.65) and an eyepiece of 10, return (400, 516.15).

title: Rocket Stage Delta Velocity
spec: Calculate the change in velocity for a single rocket stage using the Tsiolkovsky equation. Write an entry function `stage(mass, empty)` where the first is the total initial mass in kilograms and the second is the dry empty mass in kilograms. Assume a constant specific impulse of three hundred seconds and a standard gravity of nine point eight one meters per second squared. Compute the exhaust velocity by multiplying specific impulse by gravity. Then compute the delta velocity by multiplying the exhaust velocity by the natural logarithm of the ratio of initial mass to dry mass. Return the exhaust velocity and the delta velocity. Example: given mass 5000 and empty 1000, ratio is 5, exhaust is 2943, delta velocity is 4736.5.
